cards.note: Trident poletops with the tip of the middle bar bent at a 90° angle can be found in Assam.
Assamese, mainly found in Assam, also uses the Bengali script, with the addition of some characters, most notably ৰ and ৱ.
Pole paint consisting of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes can be found in Bihar.
In Bihar, and less commonly Jharkhand, you may find trees with four red and white stripes painted near the bottom.
Doum palms, which appear similar to Palmyra palms but with multiple branches, are almost exclusive to the union territory of Diu.
Flat Guna tiles is just a tiled roof full of staple-shaped tiles. It can be found around Prayagraj, south east of Uttar Pradesh state,
Flat tiles seem to be the worst type of tile by their appearance. They are mainly found in Madhya Pradesh and southern Uttar pradesh.
Concrete holey poles are unique to Gujarat and the Union territory of Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

It has “U” shape but there is a flatter shaped tile connecting tiles to each other.

It’s very common in southeastern Uttar Pradesh, western Bihar and rarely in northeastern Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.
Poles divided in two sections, in a similar fashion to Brazilian poles, are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

Kannada is found in Karnataka and has a script with a lot of smooth curves and small circles. Many characters also feature a distinct squiggly tail in the top right corner, which is less common in Telugu. It is very similar to the Telugu script(but that one has usually "checkmarks" on top of letters.
You can commonly find those small yellow pole markings in Kerala. Other states might have sometimes yellow markings like that but they are just way more rare.
Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an upside down A slightly below the top of the pole.
The Malayalam script can be found in Kerala and mostly consists of somewhat simple-looking curvy letters, often containing upside-down U-shapes.
In Manipur you can often find trident poletops on poles made entirely out of metal. They sometimes have small bars on the top of the trident.

Marathi, found in Maharashtra, also uses the Devanagari script so basically looks like hindi but if you can see the letter ळ that means it's Marathi. Sometimes you won't see that letter so don't rule out Maharashtra.

The Oriya script is found in Odisha and has a curvy look, with many letters having wide semi-circles covering the top. Many letters have a distinct diacritic in the shape of a wide curve above the top of the letter. A useful mnemonic is that the shape of the characters resembles 💀 emoji.

Electricity boxes what are mint green with small window-like squares are almost exclusive to Punjab.

You can rarely see them in Haryana

Punjabi can be found in Punjab in northwestern India. While the script looks somewhat similar to Hindi, it can generally be differentiated by the softer shape of the letters and the horizontal bar being broken over certain letters. It also has some distinctly different features, such as the letters ਨ, ਲ and ਅ.
The Tamil script is found in Tamil Nadu and has a distinct combination of curves, straight lines and 90° angles. Some letters also have diacritics shaped like dots.
Markings on poles and trees, consisting of one black stripe in-between two white ones, are common in Tamil Nadu.

Telugu, found in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh has script with a lot of smooth curves and circles. It looks similar to Kannada language but you can see a lot of distinct "checkmarks" on top of the letters.

A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down trapezoid is most common in Chhattisgarh and somewhat common in Meghalaya, Tripura and Maharashtra, but can rarely be found in many other states.

NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present.
Upside down triangle poletops placed below the top of the pole are commonly found in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and less commonly in Madhya Pradesh.

This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.

It is very common in West Bengal, eastern Jharkhand and eastern Bihar, but doesn’t go further north than Purnia, Bihar.
Small metal poletops in the shape of a window are found in Punjab(super common) and Haryana.
